text:
anya: Heads-up: ran into a warmup failure on canary where a gzipped safetensors shard had an abbreviated header and our index-first path gave up.
jon: ouch. which path did it take? index-first should fallback to streaming, right?
anya: it tried index-first -> validated checksum -> blob not found for range -> threw and bubble-up. fallback was gated behind 'manifest present' check.
sasha: that's the crux. some of our producers write a slim sidecar index that only contains offsets for uncompressed chunks. gzipped payloads still need range + inflate.
kevin: so the connector assumes index semantics that don't map to compressed blobs. we need a capability bitset on the index or a small handshake.
matt: agreed. proposal: introduce a tiny "BlobIndex v1" contract with methods: probe(), resolve_range(start,end), open_stream(range?) — probe returns supported features: [byte_ranges, gzip_streamable, signature_present].
anya: exactly. probe would be allowed to be cheap (head GET or a small metadata call). if probe says gzip_streamable=false we prefer index-first, otherwise prefer streaming-first for gzipped artifacts.
jon: tradeoffs? extra RTT for probe adds latency on cold start.
sasha: we can cache probe results per model+artifact hash. probes happen once per new bundle/version. cost is minimal compared to a failed warmup and retries.
kevin: also need to standardize signature order: verify manifest signature before streaming vs after streaming. if we stream first then verify later, we might do wasted bandwidth. if we verify header first, we need deterministic header placement.
matt: suggestion: signature in sidecar metadata (always probe-able). if present, probe returns signature_state: valid|missing|delegated. runtime can decide: if signature_state=valid then fetch ranges; if delegated, call KMS flow.
anya: implementation note: probe should be abortable and cheap, avoid full HEAD on large object stores that charge per operation. use a composite metadata object alongside blob (e.g., .meta.json) and fall back to a lightweight HEAD only if meta missing.
jon: how about mmap vs stream path selection? our mmap loader expects contiguous offset mapping which gzipped chunks break.
sasha: loader should ask BlobIndex.resolve_range for an exact list of blob segments for a logical tensor. For mmapable blobs, resolve_range returns a single contiguous segment + file descriptor. For non-mmapable, it returns segments with (blob, start, len, decompress_hint).
kevin: we must keep the hotstart path minimal: when in a high-qps hotstart, prefer a best-effort streaming prefetch that populates K/V cache without blocking inference.
matt: add a third flag in probe: background_prefetch_safe: true|false. when true, warmup scheduler can kickoff low-priority streamed prefetches.
anya: sounds good. next step: I'll drop a short RFC with the concrete protobuf-ish contract and a compatibility shim that implements probe() for our current index and catalog writers.
jon: +1. also add metrics: probe_latency, probe_miss, resolve_segments_count, fallback_count.
sasha: and an experiment: opt-in env var REDWOOD_HYBRID_BLOB_INDEX=true to test on canary before rollout.
kevin: whoever picks this up, add a small fuzz test that feeds truncated headers and compressed blobs to ensure we don't crash.
matt: I'll add it to my queue; can we get an oncall runbook entry? dev-bot: RFC created: /r/hybrid-blob-index-probe (link pinned to #eng-ml). :white_check_mark:
anya: thanks — will post the RFC link and a checklist for migration. :thumbsup:
